candidates.name: self-attention
candidates.summary: An attention mechanism in which queries, keys and values all come from the same sequence, so each position can relate to every other position in order to compute a representation of the sequence.
candidates.evidence: Self-attention, sometimes called intra-attention is an attention mechanism relating different positions of a single sequence

candidates.name: attention mechanism
candidates.summary: A function that maps a query and a set of key-value pairs to an output, computed as a weighted sum of the values where each weight comes from a compatibility function of the query with the corresponding key.
candidates.evidence: mapping a query and a set of key-value pairs to an output

candidates.name: scaled dot-product attention
candidates.summary: An attention function that computes dot products of queries with keys, divides them by $\sqrt{d_k}$, applies a softmax to get weights, and uses them to average the values: $\mathrm{softmax}(QK^T/\sqrt{d_k})V$. The scaling keeps the softmax from saturating when $d_k$ is large.
candidates.evidence: We call our particular attention "Scaled Dot-Product Attention"

candidates.name: multi-head attention
candidates.summary: Attention performed several times in parallel on different learned linear projections of queries, keys and values, with the outputs concatenated and projected again. It lets a model attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions.
candidates.evidence: allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions

candidates.name: Transformer architecture
candidates.summary: A neural sequence model architecture built from stacked attention and feed-forward layers, with no recurrence or convolution, typically in an encoder-decoder arrangement.
candidates.evidence: the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely

candidates.name: encoder-decoder architecture
candidates.summary: A model structure in which an encoder maps an input sequence to continuous representations and a decoder generates an output sequence from them, one element at a time.
candidates.evidence: Most competitive neural sequence transduction models have an encoder-decoder structure

candidates.name: sequence transduction
candidates.summary: The task of mapping an input sequence of symbols to an output sequence, as in machine translation.
candidates.evidence: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks

candidates.name: recurrent neural network
candidates.summary: A neural network that processes a sequence step by step, computing each hidden state from the previous hidden state and the current input. This sequential dependence prevents parallelization across positions.
candidates.evidence: they generate a sequence of hidden states ht, as a function of the previous hidden state ht−1 and the input for position t

candidates.name: convolutional sequence model
candidates.summary: A model that computes hidden representations in parallel for all positions using convolutions with a limited kernel width. Relating distant positions requires stacking many layers.
candidates.evidence: all of which use convolutional neural networks as basic building block

candidates.name: positional encoding
candidates.summary: Vectors added to token embeddings to give a model without recurrence or convolution information about token order. They can be fixed sinusoids of different frequencies or learned.
candidates.evidence: we add "positional encodings" to the input embeddings at the bottoms of the encoder and decoder stacks

candidates.name: masked self-attention
candidates.summary: Self-attention in which illegal connections to later positions are blocked, for example by setting their softmax inputs to $-\infty$, so predictions at a position depend only on earlier positions.
candidates.evidence: masking out (setting to −∞) all values in the input of the softmax which correspond to illegal connections

candidates.name: auto-regressive generation
candidates.summary: Producing an output sequence one element at a time, with each step conditioned on the elements already generated.
candidates.evidence: At each step the model is auto-regressive, consuming the previously generated symbols as additional input

candidates.name: residual connection
candidates.summary: A connection that adds a layer's input to its output, so that the layer computes $x + F(x)$. It eases the training of deep networks.
candidates.evidence: We employ a residual connection around each of the two sub-layers

candidates.name: layer normalization
candidates.summary: A normalization technique that standardizes the activations of a layer across the feature dimension for each example, stabilizing training.
candidates.evidence: followed by layer normalization

candidates.name: position-wise feed-forward network
candidates.summary: A small fully connected network, two linear transformations with a ReLU in between, applied identically and independently to each position of a sequence.
candidates.evidence: applied to each position separately and identically

candidates.name: softmax function
candidates.summary: A function that converts a vector of real scores into a probability distribution by exponentiating and normalizing them. Very large inputs push it into regions with tiny gradients.
candidates.evidence: apply a softmax function to obtain the weights on the values

candidates.name: BLEU score
candidates.summary: An automatic metric for machine translation quality that measures n-gram overlap between a system output and reference translations.
candidates.evidence: 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task

candidates.name: learning rate warmup
candidates.summary: A learning-rate schedule that increases the rate linearly for an initial number of steps and then decays it, for example proportionally to the inverse square root of the step number.
candidates.evidence: increasing the learning rate linearly for the first warmup_steps training steps, and decreasing it thereafter

candidates.name: Adam optimizer
candidates.summary: A stochastic gradient-based optimization method that adapts per-parameter step sizes using running estimates of the first and second moments of gradients.
candidates.evidence: We used the Adam optimizer [20] with β1 = 0.9, β2 = 0.98

candidates.name: dropout
candidates.summary: A regularization technique that randomly zeroes a fraction of activations during training to reduce overfitting.
candidates.evidence: we apply dropout [33] to the output of each sub-layer

candidates.name: label smoothing
candidates.summary: A regularization technique that replaces hard one-hot targets with softened distributions, making the model less confident. It can hurt perplexity while improving accuracy.
candidates.evidence: we employed label smoothing of value ϵls = 0.1

candidates.name: byte-pair encoding
candidates.summary: A subword tokenization method that iteratively merges the most frequent symbol pairs to build a fixed vocabulary, allowing rare words to be represented as pieces.
candidates.evidence: Sentences were encoded using byte-pair encoding [3]

candidates.name: beam search
candidates.summary: A decoding algorithm that keeps the several highest-scoring partial output sequences at each step instead of only one.
candidates.evidence: We used beam search with a beam size of 4 and length penalty α = 0.6

candidates.name: path length between long-range dependencies
candidates.summary: The number of steps signals must traverse between two positions in a network. Shorter paths make long-range dependencies easier to learn.
candidates.evidence: The third is the path length between long-range dependencies in the network

candidates.name: weight tying of embeddings
candidates.summary: Sharing one weight matrix between the input embedding, output embedding and pre-softmax linear layers to reduce parameters.
candidates.evidence: we share the same weight matrix between the two embedding layers and the pre-softmax linear transformation

candidates.name: constituency parsing
candidates.summary: The task of producing a syntactic tree that groups a sentence's words into nested phrases.
candidates.evidence: English constituency parsing

resolutions.name: Adam optimizer
resolutions.reason: Adam is a gradient-based optimizer using moment estimates, while advantage estimation is a reinforcement-learning variance-reduction technique, so they are unrelated ideas.
